key_insight: Introducing bidirectional cross-modal prompting lets event and frame processing streams exchange compact, learnable cues to close the modality gap, producing more accurate and robust asymmetric stereo depth estimates under fast motion and challenging lighting.
problem_solved: Bridges the domain gap between high-temporal-resolution event data and rich spatial frame data so asymmetric event-frame stereo no longer marginalizes one modality and fails in dynamic or low-light scenes.
method: Bidirectional Cross-Modal Prompting: learnable prompt tokens are exchanged between event and frame network branches to guide feature extraction and alignment.
AsymmetricStereo Architecture: fuse event temporal cues with frame spatial context in a stereo pipeline to estimate disparity/depth robustly under motion and poor illumination.
Cross-modal training/consistency: supervision and consistency constraints encourage prompts to align modality-specific features and improve stereo matching.
impact: Provides a practical way to combine complementary sensor modalities for reliable 3D perception in real-world, high-speed, and low-light scenarios, improving robustness for robotics, autonomous driving, and AR/VR systems.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic of asymmetric stereo rig (event camera + frame camera) showing complementary data streams

Timeline/feature visualization showing event spikes (high temporal resolution) vs. frame image (rich spatial detail)
paper_title: Bidirectional Cross-Modal Prompting for Event-Frame Asymmetric Stereo
paper_authors: Ninghui Xu, Fabio Tosi, Lihui Wang, Jiawei Han, Luca Bartolomei
